identificationModule.briefTitle: Continued Treatment With Docetaxel Versus Switch to Cabazitaxel After Minor Prostate Specific Antigen Response to Docetaxel in Patients With Castration-Resistant Metastatic Prostate Cancer
identificationModule.officialTitle: Phase II Randomized Study of Continuing Treatment With Docetaxel Versus Switching to Cabazitaxel After Minor Prostate Specific Antigen Response to Docetaxel in the First Line Treatment of Patients With Castration-Resistant Metastatic Prostate Cancer.

descriptionModule.briefSummary:
Primary Objective:

* To compare the continuation of treatment with docetaxel versus switching to cabazitaxel regarding the time to PSA (Prostatic Specific Antigen) progression (TTP-PSA), in patients with Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer (CRPC) that, after four cycles of docetaxel, have minor PSA response (defined as a reduction between 1% and 49%) or increase of up to 24% in PSA levels.

Secondary Objectives:

* PSA response rate
* Overall survival (OS)
* Incidence of Adverse Events
descriptionModule.detailedDescription: Screening: 21days (+7 days) Treatment: until PSA progression Post-treatment Follow-up: 2 years
